Hi James / Contracts Team,

Thanks — attached is a concise summary we can include in the DPA addendum. Short answers up-front, then details below.

Short summary (for contract):
- Key custody: Customer-managed keys (BYOK) are supported; Redwood will not hold unwrapped customer CMKs. We support customers hosting keys in their own cloud KMS or in a customer-provided HSM on-prem.
- Subprocessors: For a private deployment we may engage local hardware maintenance partners (listed below); such partners have limited, console-only maintenance privileges and never receive key material.
- Escrow / Break-glass: We offer an optional escrow pattern (third-party escrow agent or customer-chosen HSM escrow) and a documented break-glass process requiring multi-party authorizations and court-order/incident validation; escrow access is logged and audited.
- Evidence: We can provide SOC2 reports, KMS audit exports, and a signed maintenance attestation for every maintenance window.

Details: 
1) BYOK and runtime:
- We support two BYOK flows: (A) customer KMS (cloud-managed CMKs) with a KMS-proxy in the deployment, or (B) customer HSM locally that holds root material; Redwood's runtime retains only wrapped keys (kid references) and never stores plaintext key material.
- Runtime operations use ephemeral key-wrapping keys and hardware isolation; model payloads are encrypted at rest and decrypted within the customer's boundary.

2) Subprocessors and maintenance partners:
- Typical partners for on-site vendor maintenance include: EdgeServe Maintenance LLC (hardware swaps/RAID rebuilds) and RackOps Field Services (power/cable work). We will add both to the subprocessor appendix for Novamed.
- Access model: partners are limited to physical/firmware maintenance and a console role that cannot read disk encryption keys, keystore contents, or KMS plaintext.

3) Escrow/backstop:
- Options: (i) Third-party escrow agent (recommended) — Redwood will integrate with the agent and only provide sealed-wrapped metadata; (ii) Customer-controlled HSM on-site — vendor cannot export root material but can facilitate emergency unwrap under customer direction.
- Process: Break-glass requires three approvals (customer security lead, Redwood security lead, and legal), signed attestation, and an auditable chain-of-custody.

4) Evidence package:
- SOC2 Type II report (redacted)
- Per-maintenance attestation signed by Redwood engineer and the maintenance vendor
- KMS audit export for the relevant timeframe and operation IDs
- Console session logs and video capture (if requested and agreed in SLA)

Next steps / asks for Novamed:
- Confirm whether you want the third-party escrow option or prefer on-prem HSM escrow.
- Confirm acceptable maintenance vendors (we proposed two above).
- If you require additional contractual language (eg. specific SLAs on attestation delivery), point us to the clause and we will propose wording.

Attachments: redwood-privdep-dpa-summary-20261130.pdf (2 pages) — includes proposed DPA clause text.

I can iterate on language with legal if you share the paragraph you'd like to see. Happy to hop on a quick call this week.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Evelyn — quick technical confirmation and suggested DPA wording below. TL;DR: feasible with current runtime changes (ephemeral wrapping + strict role-based console), and we can support both escrow options.

Technical commitments we can make:
- No plaintext CMK exposure: Redwood runtime will only ever persist wrapped keys (KMS ciphertext references). For customer-hosted KMS the unwrapping operation occurs inside customer-owned KMS/HSM. For on-prem HSM, the root never leaves the HSM.
- Vendor console-only role: we will implement a sealed maintenance role that allows hardware diagnostics, firmware flashes, and component swaps but forbids any keystore or disk-unseal operations. This will be enforced by network segmentation (maintenance VLAN) and role-based access controls — maintenance sessions are proxied through a gateway with deny-list rules for KMS endpoints. 
- Escrow/backstop: support both patterns: (A) third-party escrow agent with sealed key shares; (B) on-prem HSM with documented break-glass and customer-triggered unwrap. Both will require multi-party signoff and we can log/stream the unwrap operation.
- Evidence: We can provide SOC2 report, KMS audit exports, and session logs. For forensic-level evidence (video, memory dumps) we will need an addendum and incur an agreed engineering window.

Suggested DPA clause excerpt (short):
"For Private Deployments with Customer-Managed Keys (BYOK), Redwood will not possess or access plaintext customer key material. Maintenance vendors engaged by Redwood will be granted console-only access that expressly prohibits keystore or disk-unseal operations. Break-glass access to key material will only be executed via either (a) a designated third-party escrow agent, or (b) customer-controlled on-prem HSM under written multi-party authorization; all such events will be logged and followed by a signed attestation delivered to the customer within 48 hours."

Irene / Karthik — if you see any gaps in the language above raise them now. We'll need an internal runbook for escrow unwrap steps and an SLA for the attestation delivery.

— Marcus
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

James — thanks for the patience. Per our internal review we've confirmed the following commitments for Novamed's private deployment: 

1) Key custody and runtime: Redwood will not and cannot access unwrapped customer CMKs as part of normal operations. For cloud KMS BYOK the unwrapping occurs in your KMS; for on-prem HSM the root material remains in your HSM.

2) Subprocessors & maintenance: We will include EdgeServe Maintenance LLC and RackOps Field Services in the subprocessor appendix. Both vendors will only have console-only maintenance roles. They will be network-segmented and proxied through Redwood maintenance gateways that prevent access to KMS endpoints and disk-unseal operations.

3) Escrow and break-glass: We support two options — (A) third-party escrow agent (we will integrate and manage sealed shares), or (B) on-prem HSM break-glass under customer direction. Any break-glass action requires three-party authorization and is fully logged.

4) Evidence & SLA: We will provide SOC2 Type II, KMS audit exports for relevant time windows, and a signed per-maintenance attestation within 48 hours. If Novamed requires extended forensic artifacts (memory images or session video), we can provide under a scoped addendum.

Attached is the redwood-privdep-dpa-summary-20261130.pdf with a short clause you can paste into your DPA addendum. Let me know which escrow option you prefer and whether EdgeServe / RackOps are acceptable. Once you confirm we will push the final clause to legal and provide the subprocessor appendix.
